title: Kurz von Senftenau (Hamburg) to Trauttmansdorff, 1638-39, DECODE R3811-R4736

steps.what: Fetched 9 DECODE records and 73 public images; no key record or transcription on DECODE.
Found Mírka's Crypto-World 11-12/2012 reprint: key rebuilt from R3811 p.1 interlinear, only R3811 read, key not printed.
Four agents transcribed all 73 images token by token (tr/), with the ~210 interlinear glosses on R3811 pp.1-2.
Free homophonic annealing (symbol -> letter/CV bigram/null) with a German 5-gram model on R3813.
Same with a letter-frequency (KL) penalty.
From the glosses: 41-100 are consonant+vowel signs, two consonants per ten (reverse alphabet), units o i e a; 1-40 and signs are single letters.
Structured annealer (one consonant per half, one value per single sign) seeded with 17 gloss values, on R3811-R3813, then all records.
Irregular fifth-place signs (pu lu mu hu ku du gu bu cu us ru) and two-letter single signs (te se si ve so ti tu) fixed from context and LM ranking.
All nine letters deciphered with key.json (read/*.txt); 98.3% of 22,913 cipher tokens given a value.

Checked second pass: agents compared every line of all 73 transcriptions with image crops, guided by a per-token decode; about 360 tokens corrected (c for #l-loop, 9 for #sect, 6/61 for phi, digit-group splits).
Bug fix: 56 cipher lines starting with a sign token had been skipped as comments by decode/parse; restored.
R3813 'x' is a separate crossed-f sign = ta (LM better on R3813, worse on R3812 if applied there); split out as #f-cross.
German 5-gram score per letter before/after the second pass: better on 8 of 9 letters (R4736 flat, more text restored).
alpha re-valued m -> sa (Salvius, caesaris, universal-); looped variant split out as #a-loop = m on 28 image-checked tokens; LM better on every letter vs baseline.
Clear text transcribed: R4645 Banér copies (to Lüneburg 10 Jan 1639; to Lower Saxon envoys 29 Jan 1639); R4734 endorsement shows the addressee is Count Schwarzenberg.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 22728 tokens, 133 types, de-1640s order 4: reading -2.378 per letter; random keys -4.857 (z 8.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.206 (mean -3.213, z 131.9); annealer on the real text -2.781. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): page transcriptions tr/IMG_<record>_*.txt and the machine decipherments read/<record>.txt (with the clear copy, endorsement and summary files where they exist); key key.json and KEY.md.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): the nine read/*.txt files read through. The deciphered runs are unspaced and garbled every few lines in eight letters (by-eye coherence 55-80%), so sentences that run through the cipher cannot be built: R3811-R3815, R4625, R4645, R4736 relabelled decoded, not read; R4734's short runs read (kept read, reviewed B). fraction_read 0.999 (tokens with a value) -> 0.021.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, batch b06): key corrected for all nine letters after kwic checks over the whole corpus: 38 = d (was g: feindt, und, landt, wurdt), Δ = nu (was e: warnung, hoffnung, nun, Nuncio), #dot = su (was null: sufficient, subsidia, verfassung, suspiciones), #s-long = ti (was t: militaria, resolution, obligation; glossed ti on R3811 p. 1), m = a (was null; after 29: quartier, quam, quando). Two polyphonic readings entered as relabelled signs: 9v = vo (the same 9 shape; Volck, von, vor, voluimus, darvon) and pv = vi (the crossed long-s; Salvius, resolviren, proviant, privilegia), relabelled in tr/ only where the other value gives no word. KEY.md updated.

Re-read b06: every letter checked on full-resolution crops of the DECODE images (main checkout img/; crops in the session scratchpad only, research/reading_audit/b06_crop.py); about 330 label and clear-text fixes logged in read/<rec>_corrections.tsv (φ for 6, #f-cross for p after 27, 9v, pv, regrouped figures, struck tokens turned into notes, clear Kurrent re-read, R4625 dated Hamburg 10 Feb 1639 from its p. 6). The R3811 interlinear decipherment transcribed in read/R3811_interlinear.md (it also settles 4 2 = 42, 9 = #sect, 0 = φ).

Re-read b06: readings and English translations built for all eight letters (read/<rec>_reading.md, _en.md, _reread_log.md), aligned word by word with the decode (research/reading_audit/b06_align.py; R3811 also with the interlinear gloss), supplied letters bracketed. Clean-sentence share of the reading bodies (b06_body_score.py, the _check_reading.py logic): R3811 0.62, R3812 0.616, R3815 0.681, R4625 0.603, R4645 0.625, R4736 0.636 (read, grade B); R3813 0.531, R3814 0.524 (decoded, not read: Latin, names and period spellings the word list does not know, homophone splits of x and d, runs without a word).

Re-read r2c (REREAD_BRIEF): DECODE R3813 and R3814 re-fetched with the project cookie; besides the images both list two attachments not opened before, Jakub Mírka's key reconstruction as an Excel sheet and a one-page handwritten table (2022). A key, no plaintext. Neighbouring records R3809/R3810 (Florence) and R3816/R3817 (Heusner 1637, SP 106) unrelated; web search for an edition of Kurz's Hamburg letters found none.

Our key compared with Mírka's table sign by sign: structure identical (41-100 CV table, letter series sa..vu = a..r). Two values disagreed and were checked at every occurrence in the nine letters: k = to (was ti; all 17 uses: protectorium, electores, multorum, a proposito, bis dato, in puncto ...) and m = va (was a; negativam, riserva, avantagiosen, enervatis; after 29 = qu the v is not doubled: decode.py rule). Both adopted. 4 = x does not hold for the plain 4 (fails 3 times). 9v = vo (22 Oct, flagged for review) holds at all 48 uses and is Mírka's q.

Look-alike signs split on full-resolution crops (r2c_line.py): in R3813 the crossed sign is two shapes, the tall crossed f = ta and a low curled p-form = vi (Mírka's p): 20 tokens relabelled pv, 3 plain p likewise; the looped k-form = to had been read d (8) or α (1): relabelled k; in R3811 three x are the k-form (protectorium, Stockholmb); in R3812 (5) and R3815 (1) the p after Sal- is the curled p-form; the x places of the plain 4 are a crossed 4 (Mírka's X, glossed x on R3811 p. 1), new label #4-cross = x (7); R3814: 'aber wir' (#sect), 'quod' and 'vor oder' (9v). Logged in read/<rec>_corrections.tsv. Tried without result: R3814 'auf terte freltung', 'zeit wetlohren', 'denomina-d-4-e'.

R3813 and R3814 readings updated (about 35 words now carried, aligned word by word with b06_align.py, 0 words not carried) and sibling readings brought in line with k = to, pv and #4-cross. Body scores with conjectures as holes (v2_score.py): R3813 plain 0.537 -> 0.563, explicit holes 0.910 -> 0.932; R3814 0.508 / 0.952 -> 0.968; both read as sentences: marked read (grade B). Every letter now reads: fraction_read 0.575 -> 1.0, class read.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.403; polyphony 0.0; 22 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.781

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the contemporary interlinear decipherment on p. 1 of the 17 Jan 1639 letter (R3811) and extended by homophonic solving with a German LM across all nine letters.
outcome.notes: Key complete; all nine letters deciphered (second transcription pass 21 Sept 2026). Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b06): five key values corrected for all letters after kwic checks (38 = d, Δ = nu, #dot = su, #s-long = ti, m = a) and two polyphonic readings entered as relabelled signs (9v = vo, pv = vi); about 330 label and clear-text fixes on full-resolution crops; readings and translations built for all eight letters, six of which now read (R3811, R3812, R3815, R4625, R4645, R4736; with R4734 seven of nine); R3813 and R3814 stay decoded, not read. Checks: the R3811 interlinear glosses agree with the key; R3811 matches Mírka's 2012 summary; clear text continues the deciphered sense.

outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, re-read batch b06: cipher tokens (parse.load over the corrected tr/ files) of the letters that read as sentences / all: 13618 / 23669 (R3811, R3812, R3815, R4625, R4645, R4734, R4736). Before: 0.021 (R4734 only, reading audit). Withdrawn earlier: 0.999 (tokens with a value). 23 Oct 2026, re-read r2c: R3813 (7,997) and R3814 (2,054) read too, so 23,669 / 23,669 cipher tokens are in letters that read (parse.load over the corrected tr/ files).

texts.label: R3812, Hamburg, 3 Feb 1639
texts.summary: Kurz von Senftenau on the quartering of six imperial regiments and the Lower Saxon Kreistag: Banér's plundering will ruin the Stift Halberstadt, Duke Georg of Lüneburg will not resist; he sees no real Swedish or French wish for peace and great ill-feeling between Denmark and Sweden. Postscript on Arnim's visit after escaping Swedish captivity.

reading_review.note: Hamburg, 3 Feb 1639. Read and translated; clean share 0.616 (141 of 229). Holes: about 78 [...] and 37 [?], mostly runs that do not make words after the image check and blots on I23113, I23121, I23122; the clear postscript (I23119 left) and the clear leaf I23123 are not transcribed. Rests on the key decode (key.json as corrected 22 Oct 2026: 38 = d, Δ = nu, #dot = su, #s-long = ti, m = a) of the tr/ transcription after the label fixes in read/<rec>_corrections.tsv, made on full-resolution crops of the DECODE images; words separated and the reading aligned word by word with the decode (b06_align.py), supplied letters and words bracketed.

texts.label: R3811, Hamburg, 17 Jan 1639
texts.summary: Nothing can be done with Duke Georg; France, Sweden and Holland plan an embassy to the King of Denmark to prevent a congress in Sweden; Duke August of Saxe-Lauenburg is said to seek Danish protection; Arnim denies plotting against the Peace of Prague and Kurz advises a protectorium. The letter carries an interlinear decipherment (summarised by Mírka in 2012).

reading_review.note: Hamburg, 17 Jan 1639. Read and translated (read/R3811_reading.md, _en.md); clean-sentence share of the reading body 0.62 (49 of 79 sentences). The contemporary interlinear decipherment on p. 1 and the first eleven lines of I23100 left is transcribed in read/R3811_interlinear.md and carries ex, virium, ist and subsidia where the key does not. Holes: about five clear Kurrent words, [?protectorium] and [?Stockholmb] (x = to), [?Stecknitz], [?ettlis], and the postscript in Kurz's cursive. Rests on the key decode (key.json as corrected 22 Oct 2026: 38 = d, Δ = nu, #dot = su, #s-long = ti, m = a) of the tr/ transcription after the label fixes in read/<rec>_corrections.tsv, made on full-resolution crops of the DECODE images; words separated and the reading aligned word by word with the decode (b06_align.py), supplied letters and words bracketed.

texts.label: R3813, Hamburg, 27 Jan 1639
texts.summary: Twenty-page memorandum: the enemy advances unopposed towards Salzwedel; a Kreistag broken up by the enemy is better than one concluded with express neutrality; Kurz advises a defensive strategy, distrusts Salvius, weighs a secret particular treaty with Sweden through Brandenburg or Denmark, and says France wants Lorraine, Alsace and even the imperial crown.

reading_review.note: Hamburg, 27 Jan 1639. Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (r2c): reading body (header and Notes cut) 0.563 clean sentences on the word list, 0.932 on explicit holes with every [?word] and [word] counted as a hole (v2_score.py; 290 of 311 sentences), hole rate 0.036; German of 1639 with Latin, so the explicit-hole share is the bar, and the sentences hold through the twenty pages (Banér's crossing, Duke Georg's passivity, the defensive plan, quarters against money, Salvius, the Cologne congress, the protectorium). Rests on the key decode (key.json; k = to and m = va checked against Jakub Mírka's key table attached to DECODE R3813) after 110 label and clear-text fixes on full-resolution crops (read/R3813_corrections.tsv; 32 on 23 Oct: the curled p-form = vi and the looped k-form = to split from the crossed ta-sign and d, the crossed 4 = x); b06_align.py: every unbracketed word carried by the figures or the clear text. Open: about 20 [?] words and the clerk's slips listed in the reading's Notes.

texts.label: R3814, undated, 1639
texts.summary: The Swedish agent Mithoff and the Danish mediation; safe-conducts; Lorraine, Mantua and Pomerania in pledge; Rákóczi said to take French money with the Turk's consent; Kurz defends his secret particular dealing with Mithoff and describes a secret post route via Ehrenberg and Wolfenbüttel.

reading_review.note: Undated, early 1639. Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (r2c): reading body 0.508 clean sentences on the word list (half the letter is Latin), 0.968 on explicit holes with conjectures as holes (v2_score.py; 61 of 63), hole rate 0.041; the sentences hold (the satisfactio coronae points, Salvius fooling Mithoff, the secret correspondence via Nuremberg and Wolfenbüttel). Rests on the key decode (key.json, checked against Mírka's key table on DECODE R3814) after 43 label fixes on the images (read/R3814_corrections.tsv; 23 Oct: 'aber wir' #sect, 'quod' and 'vor oder hinter Pomeren' 9v); b06_align.py 0 words not carried. Open: about 12 runs whose legible figures make no word, and the p. 4 postscript in Kurz's cursive (illegible at DECODE resolution, outside the body).

texts.label: R3815, Hamburg, 6 Feb 1639, to Ferdinand III
texts.summary: The King of Denmark is perplexed and perhaps stalling to avoid a conjunction with the Emperor; the Danish Reichsrat is irresolute; with 8-9,000 men the princes could deal with a starved, exhausted enemy; Salis sent to Hildesheim, Duke Georg, the Kreis resolution, Hatzfeldt.

reading_review.note: Hamburg, 6 Feb 1639, to Ferdinand III (pages run P1 right, P3, P2). Read and translated; clean share 0.681 (32 of 47); much of the share is the clear German framing the cipher. About fifteen single-occurrence runs stay unread (listed in the reading's Notes). Rests on the key decode (key.json as corrected 22 Oct 2026: 38 = d, Δ = nu, #dot = su, #s-long = ti, m = a) of the tr/ transcription after the label fixes in read/<rec>_corrections.tsv, made on full-resolution crops of the DECODE images; words separated and the reading aligned word by word with the decode (b06_align.py), supplied letters and words bracketed.

texts.label: R4625, Hamburg, 10 Feb 1639, to Trauttmansdorff
texts.summary: Memorandum on keeping the Lower Saxon Circle divided and holding Halberstadt, Magdeburg, Hildesheim and Wolfenbüttel; 8,000 Danish men in Holstein; three grades of Circle war; the imperial army is ruined.

reading_review.note: Memorandum dated on p. 6 "Hamburg den 10. Febr. Ao 1639" (read 22 Oct 2026; the label said undated), with a clear covering letter on p. 7. Read and translated; clean share 0.603 (70 of 116). About 20 [...] and 15 [?] remain; the p. 5 Latin is the weakest part. Rests on the key decode (key.json as corrected 22 Oct 2026: 38 = d, Δ = nu, #dot = su, #s-long = ti, m = a) of the tr/ transcription after the label fixes in read/<rec>_corrections.tsv, made on full-resolution crops of the DECODE images; words separated and the reading aligned word by word with the decode (b06_align.py), supplied letters and words bracketed.

texts.label: R4645, Hamburg, 13 Feb 1639
texts.summary: The Danish interposition and a possible conjunction with the Emperor: the King's distinctions proved mere lies; Count Pentz says the King must drop the mediation and denounce Sweden. With clear copies of two letters of Banér of 29 Jan 1639.

reading_review.note: Hamburg, 13 Feb 1639 (letter order P9, P1, P2, P6; the Banér copies are clear, read/R4645_clear.md). Read and translated; clean share 0.625 (20 of 32). A leaf between P2 and P6 is not among the DECODE images; the P6 close and postscript in Kurz's cursive and one Latin run on P9 are unread. Rests on the key decode (key.json as corrected 22 Oct 2026: 38 = d, Δ = nu, #dot = su, #s-long = ti, m = a) of the tr/ transcription after the label fixes in read/<rec>_corrections.tsv, made on full-resolution crops of the DECODE images; words separated and the reading aligned word by word with the decode (b06_align.py), supplied letters and words bracketed.

texts.label: R4734, 8 Apr 1639, copy

reading_review.note: read/R4734.txt: a copy with short cipher runs inside clear German; the runs read and join the clear text into sentences ("was expirante interpositione fur ein weeg zu ergreifen zu dem lieben Frieden"; "bis jede forma coniunctionis versichert"). The clear lines marked [... not transcribed] are clear text left out, not cipher holes.

texts.summary: The Danish mediation has expired and the King has his hands tied; the Lower Saxon Circle must contribute to war or to compensation; Stralsund or other lands might go to Brandenburg. Addressed to 'E. Excell.' (Schwarzenberg per DECODE).

texts.label: R4736, Glückstadt, 14 Apr 1639
texts.summary: At the Danish court: the Danes complain that war in Austria is bought with peace in Lower Saxony while the Swedes stay in Mecklenburg and Pomerania; papers to be sent to Schwarzenberg; outward respect for the Emperor nowhere greater than at Glückstadt.

reading_review.note: Glückstadt, 14 Apr 1639. Read and translated; clean share 0.636 (28 of 44). Open: a few Latin and Italian runs ("quid consilii [...] armorum", "alli altri [?scoppa]", "lentra i gnadi"), the postscript and margin note in Kurz's cursive. Rests on the key decode (key.json as corrected 22 Oct 2026: 38 = d, Δ = nu, #dot = su, #s-long = ti, m = a) of the tr/ transcription after the label fixes in read/<rec>_corrections.tsv, made on full-resolution crops of the DECODE images; words separated and the reading aligned word by word with the decode (b06_align.py), supplied letters and words bracketed.
